correctness.rationale: For odd field order, unit commutation is exactly vanishing of odd-part wedge product. This gives centralizer index \(q^{r}\) with \(r\) the rank of odd-to-even wedge multiplication. An odd element with nonzero degree-one term is carried by a filtered exterior-algebra automorphism to a basis generator, giving rank eight. If the linear term vanishes, the cubic term defines an alternating bilinear form on five coordinates; all ranks are \(0,2,4\), and exact counts follow by choosing the radical and a symplectic form on its quotient. The total weighted mass is \(q^{31}\). In characteristic two exterior multiplication is commutative. Independent exact computations from packaged `verify.py` passed, including complete \(3^{10}\) alternating-form enumeration and direct associative multiplication tests. No finite test is used as an infinite proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Maximal subalgebra classifications do not enumerate centralizer ranks of every algebra element. Rossmann’s polynomial is for graphical groups with independent edge-commutator directions; it does not immediately specialize to the exterior unit group with degree-one/degree-three cross products. Indeed, the latter has a fifteen-dimensional quotient by its center and fifteen-dimensional derived subgroup, with noncentral conjugacy exponents only 2,4,8. A graphical group with those dimensions would need fifteen nonisolated vertices and fifteen edges; every vertex must then have degree at least two, forcing disjoint cycles. Choosing a group element with all vertex coordinates nonzero would yield commutator rank at least ten, impossible in the current group. Hence even an abstract graphical-group identification cannot furnish this formula. The four-generator associative-commutator precedent does not imply a five-generator alternating rank-four stratum.

value.rationale: The class-size distribution of the canonical principal-unit group of a familiar finite-dimensional local algebra is a standard, intrinsic finite-group invariant. Five generators are the first odd exterior rank where degree-three data give both rank-two and rank-four alternating forms; the complete classification of a group with \(q^{31}\) elements provides all multiplicities, a forbidden class-size exponent six, exact center and class-two behavior, plus a sharp characteristic-two collapse. This goes beyond repeating the known exterior identities or tabulating a few numerical cases.
